title: Dukkah
subtitle: Egyptian nut and spice blend for dipping
excerpt: The Egyptian spice and nut mixture that has become one of the most useful pantry condiments to arrive in British kitchens: toasted hazelnuts ground with coriander seeds, cumin, and sesame into a coarse, fragrant blend for dipping bread in olive oil and then into the dukkah.

recipe.sourceNotes: Dukkah (also written duqqa, from the Arabic for pounding) is an Egyptian condiment and street food with a history stretching back centuries. It is sold in Egyptian markets wrapped in newspaper cones or paper bags and eaten for breakfast or as a snack: flat bread is dipped first in olive oil, then pressed into the dukkah, coating the bread in the fragrant, crunchy mixture. The specific blend of nuts and spices varies by maker and family, but hazelnuts, coriander seed, cumin, and sesame are consistent core elements. Dukkah arrived in the British food consciousness largely through food writers such as Claudia Roden (who documented Egyptian food in exhaustive detail) and has become widely used as a dip, a salad topping, and a crust for fish and lamb. The mixture should remain coarse: a fine powder has lost what makes dukkah distinctive.

content.text: Toast each ingredient separately: coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and sesame seeds all have different toasting times and will burn if done together. Process to a coarse crumb, not a fine powder; there should be visible pieces of nut. Store in a sealed jar for up to 2 weeks. Serve with a bowl of good olive oil and flatbread for dipping.

Toast the hazelnuts in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, tossing frequently, until golden. Tip into a clean tea towel and rub to remove most of the skins (for skin-on nuts). Toast the coriander seeds for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant, then the cumin seeds for 1 minute, then the sesame seeds for 1 to 2 minutes until pale golden. Let all the ingredients cool completely.

Pulse the cooled hazelnuts in a food processor or blender briefly to a coarse crumb. Do not over-process. Add the toasted spices, sesame seeds, salt, and pepper. Pulse 3 to 4 more times until just combined but still very coarse and textured. Taste and adjust the salt. Store in a sealed jar at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.
